title: Battery parasitic draw test (dead battery overnight)
warnings: Don't crank the engine or turn on high-draw items with the meter in series. It will blow the meter fuse.
Modules on modern cars take 20-60+ minutes to go to sleep. Opening a door wakes them back up.
steps: Charge and load-test the battery first. A bad battery can look like a draw.
Key off, all doors closed. Defeat hood and door switches (latch the door latches with a screwdriver) so you can work with doors open.
Meter on 10 A DC. Connect in series between the negative battery post and the negative cable, then remove the cable while keeping the meter connected so modules don't reset.
Wait for the modules to sleep (watch the reading drop). Then switch to the mA range if the reading is low enough.
Typical acceptable draw: under 50 mA on most cars (older cars with no modules: near zero).
If high, pull fuses one at a time and watch for the drop. Or measure millivolts across each fuse (no pulling, so modules stay asleep) and compare with a fuse voltage-drop chart.
Once the circuit is found, unplug components on it one at a time (common: glovebox/trunk lights, aftermarket stereo, stuck relay, alternator diode).
Also test the alternator: disconnect its output wire. If the draw disappears, the diode is leaking.
